headline: Foundation models and registration tools link microscopy to single-cell spatial data
label: Single Cell Spatial Imaging Analysis
summary: Foundation models and denoisers for multiplexed and histology images now reach single-cell and 3D tissue resolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational extraction of single-cell and tissue-level information from microscopy and histology images. SAM2 extends a segmentation foundation model to joint 2D and 3D light and electron microscopy, while Loki2 applies a single-cell pathology foundation model, trained on UniSeg with 15M cells, to H&E images to recover transcriptomic and protein signals. sc-HistoMorphomics profiles 194 nuclear features in H&E whole-slide images and links them to spatial transcriptomics, and GenVinci reconstructs 3D tissue from histology to map senescence. Registration and denoising steps support these analyses: MeXalign coregisters LA-ICP-TOFMS and immunofluorescence via single-cell masks, SpillOT removes spillover in multiplexed images, and Space-map aligns serial sections into 3D atlases. A kidney benchmark with 543 annotated tiles provides a public reference for segmentation methods. The recurring novelty is extending single-cell resolution to 3D and multimodal inference directly from routine stains.
